relations.definition: To be situated or positioned within a particular geographic area or boundaries.
relations.embedding_query_text: located in: To be situated or positioned within a particular geographic area or boundaries.

chosen_property.label: containedIn
chosen_property.justification: Best match among candidates for both instances.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: longitude
candidates.comment: A longitude relation between geographic coordinates or a place and its longitudinal value. Also called: geographic longitude, east-west coordinate, meridian position. Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".

candidates.label: latitude
candidates.comment: A geographical coordinate relation between geo-coordinates or a place and its north-south position on the Earth's surface. Also called lat, north-south coordinate, parallel. Examples: GeoCoordinates have a latitude of '34.0522'. A place has a latitude of '-33.8688'. The city's latitude is '40.7128'. Distinct from longitude, which is the east-west position.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: geoMidpoint
candidates.comment: A geo midpoint relation between a geo circle and the geographical coordinates representing its center. Also called: center coordinates, geographic center, central point. Examples: "Circular Search Area" geo midpoint "Latitude: 34.0, Longitude: -118.0", "GeoCircle around City" geo midpoint "City Center Coordinates", "Radar Range" geo midpoint "Radar Station Location".

chosen_property.justification: Flipped to inverse to match subject-object direction.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: specialCommitments
candidates.comment: A description of any specific commitments or considerations associated with a job posting. Also called "job commitments", "employment considerations", "special hiring programs". Examples: "The job posting has specialCommitments VeteranCommit", "This role includes specialCommitments for military spouses", "The company lists specialCommitments for diversity initiatives."

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: funder
candidates.comment: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: accountablePerson
candidates.comment: An accountable person relation between a creative work and the individual legally responsible for it. Also called legally responsible person, liable party, responsible individual. Examples: "A news article's accountable person is its editor-in-chief.", "A company report's accountable person is the CEO."

candidates.label: sponsor

Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Also called hospital data, reporting dataset, healthcare metrics. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: diversityStaffingReport
candidates.comment: A diversity staffing report relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and an article or URL containing a report on staffing diversity issues. Also called "staff diversity report", "workforce diversity data", "inclusion metrics report". Examples: "News media organization diversityStaffingReport 'Article on newsroom diversity'", "Company diversityStaffingReport 'URL to annual diversity report'", "Organization diversityStaffingReport 'Self-reported staffing data'".

candidates.label: cvdFacilityCounty
candidates.comment: A geographical identification relation between a CDCPMD record and the county of the NHSN facility it applies to. Also called: facility county, hospital county, reporting county. Examples: "COVID-19 Data" cvd facility county "Los Angeles County", "NHSN Record" cvd facility county "Cook County", "Hospital Report" cvd facility county "King County". Distinct from cvdFacilityId, which is the identifier of the facility.

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: cvdNumVentUse
candidates.comment: An occupancy relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of mechanical ventilators currently in use. Also called: ventilators in use, occupied ventilators, ventilator usage. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num vent use "70", "Facility B Report" cvd num vent use "30", "Medical Center C" cvd num vent use "150". Distinct from cvdNumVent, which is the total number of ventilators available.

candidates.label: cvdNumBedsOcc
candidates.comment: An occupancy relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of staffed inpatient beds that are occupied. Also called: occupied inpatient beds, bed occupancy count, current bed usage. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num beds occ "450", "Facility B Report" cvd num beds occ "200", "Medical Center C" cvd num beds occ "800". Distinct from cvdNumBeds, which is the total number of beds.

chosen_property.label: byDay
chosen_property.justification: Best match for specifying the day of occurrence.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.
